body:
Re-files the doctor half of T-01KYSC1SQ2CBDDXVM16N000PYE, which PR #509 annotated `completed: true` while sweeping "42 shipped railless tickets". That sweep matched on a ticket having no rails — a statement about privilege, not about whether the work shipped. Re-filed rather than un-completed because `rail-freeze` permits ADDING `completed: true` to a base ticket and nothing else, so removing it needs a maintainer override while a new ticket needs no ceremony.

=== WHAT IS STILL MISSING, MEASURED ON 86a5e75d ===

`docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md` §12 AC10 requires that doctor report orphaned anchors and stale lineage tokens, read-only. `doctorTicketStore` in `packages/tickets/lib/doctor.mjs` currently emits these checks and no others:

  active-store · archive · current-ticket · storehash-manifest-bind · transactions · writer-lock

A grep for `orphan` across `packages/tickets` and `packages/gate-manifest` returns nothing, so neither condition is reported anywhere.

=== WHAT HAS SHIPPED SINCE, AND IS THEREFORE NOT IN THIS TICKET ===

The original bundled a documentation criterion: `docs/tools/gate-manifest.md` had zero mentions of `manifest.d/`, forest, or segment. It now carries about 60 across those terms, so that half is done and this ticket is only the doctor check. That is also why this is filed as one narrower ticket rather than a re-file of the original text.

=== WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW THAN WHEN FIRST FILED ===

The manifest root is frozen and every new gate record mints a segment under `.adlc/manifest.d/`, so anchors and `.lineage` tokens are load-bearing on every branch rather than on a few. An orphaned anchor or a stale token is currently invisible until something downstream fails to resolve a segment, and the failure surfaces far from the cause.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `doctorTicketStore` gains a read-only check reporting a segment whose anchor names a root seq or another segment's line that no longer exists. verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='manifest'`
- The same check reports a `.lineage` token whose named segment no longer exists, and one whose cached ULID no longer matches the segment file on disk. verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='manifest'`
- Both conditions are REPORTED and never repaired: a doctor run over a repo with both faults leaves every file byte-identical, asserted by hashing the store and the manifest before and after. verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='manifest'`
- A healthy forest reports the new check as ok, so the check cannot pass by always firing. verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor.test.mjs`
- The tests bite: each fault case fails against the current implementation, asserted against a fixture rather than by inspection. verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor.test.mjs`
- The existing doctor suite stays green and its current check names are unchanged, since `adlc ticket doctor` output is read by operators and by ticket-store tooling. verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/*.test.mjs`
- The three CI gates pass on a freshly fetched base. verify: `npm run preflight`

allow-suppression: none

=== SURFACES THIS LEAVES ALONE ===

Repair of either fault. Doctor is read-only by the convention already stated in that file, and a repair path for anchors would need its own design — the migration and recovery ceremonies own that ground.

The chain-integrity checks (`MANIFEST_MALFORMED`, `MANIFEST_CHAIN_INVALID`, `MANIFEST_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `SEGMENT_AMBIGUOUS`) already exist and answer a different question: whether what IS there verifies, rather than whether something it points at is gone.
title: doctor reports neither an orphaned anchor nor a stale lineage token
